full_judgment:
Mr. Altaf Hossain Khan, J: This Rule was issued at the instance of victim petitioner Jasmin Nahar calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the order of Judicial custody dated 9.7.2000 passed by the learned Magistrate, First Class, Khulna in Khulna P.S. Case No. 15 dated 14.5.2000, G.R. No. 408 of 2000 corresponding to Nari-O-Shisu Case No. 94 of 2000 should not be declared illegal and improper. 

 2. The short fact leading to this Criminal Miscellaneous Case is that S.M. Lutfar Rahman as informant lodged a written ejahar on 14.5.2000 with Khulna Police Station mentioning provision of Nari-O-Shisu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 stating inter alia that Jasmin Nahar, the victim petitioner has disappeared from SOS Harman Minor School on 10.5.2000 at about 12 O Clock & thereby the informant was inspired to file a Diary being Diary Number 740 dated 11.5.2000 with the Khulna Police Station. 

 That the victim petitioner was arrested on 9.7.2000 in connection with Khulna P.S. case No. 15 dated 14.5.2000 and produced before the learned Magistrate. First Class, Khulna. The learned Magistrate was pleased to send her to judicial custody. 

 3. That thereafter the victim petitioner made a statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in which a short history of her past life has aptly described and in the said statement she did not bring any allegation against the accused persons of this case in respect of offence mentioned in the charge sheet. The victim petitioner also said in that statement that she went to the house of Hafeza Khatoon voluntarily at her will, under whose care the victim petitioner was brought up and said Hafeza Khatoon took the petitioner of her own care while the petitioner was a girl of 5 days only and there the petitioner used to call her as Ammu. It appears from the statement that in the midst of alleged danger the petitioner was unmoved. 

 4. That on 15.11.2000 a petition was moved for releasing the victim petitioner from the judicial custody but that prayer was rejected by the learned Sessions Judge and Nari-O-Shisu Adalat as an accused of this case wants to be a custodian of the petitioner and thus the cause arose to prefer this Criminal Miscellaneous Case under Section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the Rule. 

 5. That the cardinal question of the instant case is required to be determined whether the victim girl had attained the age of 18 years or not. 

 6. That the learned Advocate Mr. Binod Kumar Agarwala appearing for the petitioner submits that the victim petitioner is not an accused in the case and she is sui-juris who voluntarily went to the house of Hafeza Khatoon and as such keeping her under Judicial custody against her will is illegal, malafide, motivated and without jurisdiction and the order of Judicial custody should be set aside. The learned Advocate further submits that her age is in between 17 to 18 years according to the medical examination report. The learned Advocate referred to a case of Tarapada Sarker Vs State reported in 49 DLR page 360. 

 This Section of 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure can be invoked against illegal detention or any body detained in custody illegally. The petitioner of this case was not detained in custody illegally, she is in Judicial custody under the order of the learned Court. 

 8. However we do not find any substance in the argument made by the learned Deputy Attorney General-because of the fact that the petitioner has challenged the order of Judicial custody under the provision of 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure considering the impugned order is some kind of detention passed under the veneer of Judicial custody as the order which is under challenged does not bear the legal acumen to its true sense. Indeed there are ingredients of Section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for filing the present Criminal Miscellaneous Case, the intended provision of Section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is to secure justice for those who are detained in illegally & the present case fall within the ambit of Section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, as such the only course is open to the petitioner for getting remedy under the provision of Section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In pursuance to the above principle there are many decisions of both the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and of the High Court Division, reference may be made to the decisions reported in 51 DLR. (AD) page 238, 49 DLR page 360. 

 12. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case we find that the learned court below manifestly erred in rejecting the prayer for release of the petitioner from the Judicial custody and considering all those perspective of the case we are of the view that to keep the victim petitioner is Judicial custody against her will is unlawful. 

 15. In the circumstances we are inclined to release the victim petitioner from the Judicial custody on her own bond and accordingly the Rule issued in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7782 of 2000 is made absolute. The victim petitioner now detained in judicial custody in Khulna in connection with Khulna Police Station Case No. 15 dated 14.5.2000 be released and set free to go wherever she likes and the order of judicial custody dated 9.7.2000 passed in Khulna Police Station Case No. 15 dated 14.5.2000, G.R. Case No. 408 of 2000 corresponding to Nari-O-Shisu Case No. 34 of 2000 by the learned Magistrate, First Class, Khulna is set aside.
